# Vendored Yuxi source

Source: https://github.com/xerrors/Yuxi

Version: `v0.7.3`

Commit: `caff3208c9db9128aa0b277bc5c669141383ddbd`

The Python source under `package/yuxi/knowledge` (62 files), `package/yuxi/models` (10 files), and `package/yuxi/permissions` (2 files) is vendored from the local upstream checkout. A source comparison against the recorded v0.7.3 commit, normalizing line endings, found 59/62 knowledge files, 10/10 model files, and 2/2 permission files identical; three knowledge files have small local patches. Dify and Notion re-raise upstream request failures instead of returning an indistinguishable empty result, knowledge implementation classes load lazily so using read-only connectors does not import the optional Milvus client, and mindmap infrastructure imports are deferred until their service-bound functions run. Geo RAG Studio actively calls the upstream Dify and Notion connectors, `OtherEmbedding`, chunk parsers, OCR parser classes, reranker wire protocols, provider templates, and retrieval evaluation metrics through local adapters. The external knowledge-base API also calls Yuxi's `KnowledgeBase.build_search_output`, `_build_open_file_window`, and `_build_find_file_windows` helpers directly, together with the upstream content-hash helper for duplicate upload rejection; local SQLite metadata and parsed blocks supply the source data. The chunk adapter adds PDF source-location metadata and validates knowledge-base chunk settings. Local MinIO and Redis shims report those optional services unavailable; provider credentials remain in the SQLite registry.

Geo RAG's FastAPI routes in `app/yuxi_compat.py` are local adapters, not verbatim copies of Yuxi's `backend/server/routers` modules. A method-and-path comparison against Yuxi v0.7.3's knowledge, external knowledge, evaluation, graph, and knowledge-dashboard routers found all 77 operations represented. This verifies route surface only; it does not establish equivalent behavior for every operation.

The document lifecycle now calls the vendored `resolve_processing_params` and `params_for_uploaded_document` helpers directly. Per-request parameters override stored file parameters, which override knowledge-base defaults; effective chunk settings and OCR selection are persisted with the document. Reindexing without parameters retains the file settings, while `index-pending` forwards its native frontend parameters. The upload-only `documents/add` endpoint preserves `uploaded` status without parsing or indexing and returns Yuxi's `items`, `failed_items`, `added`, `failed`, and partial-failure contract. Parse, index, and ingest operations now return task IDs; SQLite persists queued/running/terminal task state, and a local single-worker executor performs the work and serves Yuxi-shaped task list/detail/cancel/delete APIs. This covers the embedded frontend's task lifecycle, but does not migrate Yuxi's PostgreSQL + ARQ/Redis distributed queue, leases, or multi-worker ownership semantics.

The native file table now receives Yuxi's `error_parsing`, `error_indexing`, and `indexing` status projections while Geo's internal lifecycle retains `failed`, `chunking`, and `embedding`. Failure phase and error text are persisted; a successful retry removes the old error. Native statistics include folder rows and `pending_index_count`, and bulk indexing selects both parsed files and files with an indexing failure. Bulk parsing selects uploaded files, matching the upstream pending-parse policy.

Scoped Embedding/Reranker configuration does not fall back field-by-field to global `.env` identity fields. Blank endpoint/model disables the scoped provider even when a stored credential remains; missing credentials do not inherit a global key. A selected `provider_id:model_id` resolves the registered provider's own endpoint and credential. An unscoped provider probe with omitted identity fields may use `.env`; explicit blank identity fields remain blank.

After these fixes, on 2026-10-03 the Python suite passed 88 tests and compilation passed. Real requests through authenticated Java `:8007` verified a corrupt PDF's parse failure and an unavailable loopback embedding endpoint's indexing failure; clearing the scoped endpoint/model then retrying pending indexing succeeded and removed the error. A fresh run of the 49-page PDF produced 1,008 blocks, 67 chunks, five final evidences and 1,840 context characters. Vector and Reranker counts were zero because no model provider was enabled; this is BM25 validation, not full model-chain acceptance.

Native document deletion now handles folders recursively, matching `KnowledgeBase.delete_folder`'s descendant-first order. Folder basic-info requests return actual folder metadata. Batch deletion returns upstream-shaped `{doc_id, error}` failures, reports partial success, and returns HTTP 400 when every requested item fails. With the Milvus backend enabled, file deletion removes its index before deleting local metadata and source; an index failure preserves those local records. Milvus deletion ordering and failure preservation were unit-tested with a replaced adapter; live Milvus deletion and graph snapshot cleanup are not yet acceptance-proven.

On 2026-10-03, the Python suite passed 100 tests and compilation passed. A fresh authenticated Java-gateway fixture verified folder movement, HTTP 400 for self/descendant cycles, recursive deletion, zero remaining rows/chunks/evidence, structured partial failure, and HTTP 400 for total failure. Deletion and incremental mindmap pruning directly call the vendored `remove_files_from_mindmap`; AST comparison confirmed that it, `_prune_mindmap_node`, `_collect_leaf_filenames`, and `detect_mindmap_changes` match local Yuxi functions. Six isolated tests cover single/batch/folder deletion and preservation of preexisting content staleness. A real gateway deletion also pruned a manually seeded saved-tree fixture while retaining the other file and an up-to-date source fingerprint. These checks prove tree synchronization, not LLM generation. Provider probe unit tests verify resolved model names and protocol reporting for registry selections; no live model request was enabled.

Further source comparison verified that Geo calls Yuxi's mindmap file-list formatter, leaf-name change detector, full/incremental prompt builders, JSON parser, and file-count/page-size constants unchanged. The mindmap file endpoint now returns the native `{files,total,truncated}` envelope and includes uploaded files. Legacy trees without stored file IDs are reconciled by leaf filename; direct deletion prunes those trees too. Generation uses Yuxi's 200-file cap and incremental no-change behavior. Tests assert upstream prompt bytes/structures at the call boundary with a unit model response; this is not a live LLM generation result. The change detector uses the native 500-file window and retains tracked files beyond it. On 2026-10-03, the expanded Python suite passed 107 tests and `compileall` passed. Live `:8010` probes against the real 1,528,947-byte PDF returned 49 pages and 1,008 PyMuPDF blocks with bboxes; direct local ingestion indexed it and keyword retrieval returned 38 BM25 candidates, three final evidences, and 2,000 context characters. Embedding and Reranker live probes reported unavailable (HTTP 503) because no provider API configuration is present. The latest Java-gateway recheck was not completed: local Docker Desktop failed while removing its inaccessible `AppData/Local/docker-secrets-engine/engine.sock`, so the project's Redis `:26379` and Java `:8007` could not start.

On 2026-10-03, the Python suite passed 81 tests and compilation passed. A real 1,528,947-byte, 49-page PDF was uploaded, parsed and indexed through the authenticated Java `:8007` gateway to RAG `:8010`. Its knowledge-base default remained 512 tokens while a file override of 256 tokens / 0% overlap produced 67 chunks; all 67 chunk texts matched a direct call to the vendored Yuxi dispatcher. Reindexing without overrides also produced 67 chunks. Keyword retrieval returned 50 BM25 candidates and five final evidences with 1,840 context characters. All five page/bbox pairs matched stored source spans and contained text within the actual PDF. This proves the tested lifecycle and configuration behavior, not complete knowledge-base parity. Embedding, Reranker and MinerU provider probes returned HTTP 503 `unavailable` because their services/credentials were not configured; the local PyMuPDF probe returned 49 pages and 1,008 blocks with bboxes.

To complete the vendored knowledge package's internal source dependencies, 25 supporting Python files were copied unchanged from the same Yuxi checkout: configuration, repositories, OCR/task services, MinIO/Postgres/Neo4j adapters, and utilities. SHA-256 hashes matched the upstream working tree after copying. The Geo-local MinIO import shim remains active in place of Yuxi's service-bound package initializer, while exposing the migrated MinIO client modules as optional submodules. The upstream `MilvusKB` class is vendored and importable but is not the active Geo pipeline class: its indexing lifecycle uses Yuxi's PostgreSQL file/chunk repositories, model registry, and MinIO-backed parsed files. Geo instead keeps source files, parsed blocks, chunk metadata, and provider configuration in its own local SQLite/filesystem layer and calls a Geo-owned Milvus adapter when `RAG_SEARCH_BACKEND=milvus`.

Parser files are from the same v0.7.3 source commit. OCR integrations use the upstream RapidOCR, MinerU, PP-Structure, DeepSeek OCR, and PaddleOCR classes when their required local packages, endpoints, credentials, and (where relevant) image storage support are present. Missing providers are reported as unavailable; no parser result is synthesized.

License: MIT, copied from the upstream root `LICENSE` file in this directory.

The active Geo pipeline selects its index with `RAG_SEARCH_BACKEND`: `sqlite` uses the local BM25/vector fallback, while `milvus` writes and retrieves chunks from a project-owned Milvus collection. The active Milvus adapter uses the same Chinese analyzer, BM25 Function, COSINE vector metric, IVF_FLAT vector index, sparse DAAT_MAXSCORE index, query parameters, and Milvus 2.5.6 `WeightedRanker` as Yuxi. It adds Geo-specific per-knowledge-base hashed collection names and a `has_embedding` filter so BM25-only documents can coexist with embedded chunks. Geo's separate SQLite document/chunk metadata remains the source for evidence text, page/bbox spans, and local file filters. The active code is therefore behavior-aligned at the Milvus query layer, but is not a direct runtime invocation of Yuxi's `MilvusKB` class. We have not established full functional parity for every Yuxi knowledge-base operation or identical ranking against the live Yuxi service; PostgreSQL, Redis, Neo4j, and Yuxi's Docker harness have not been reintroduced.

Evaluation dataset generation now supports Yuxi's `graph_enhanced` mode. It selects anchor chunks that have local `Chunk` nodes and `MENTIONS` entity edges, validates the persisted graph fingerprint against the currently indexed SQLite documents/chunks, then expands context with the vendored Yuxi seed-subgraph and personalized PageRank helpers. The Yuxi graph expansion top-k bounds, PPR damping, node cap, and 0.9 round seed decay are carried into the local graph path; `graph_expand_top_k` is preserved from the Yuxi API payload through the task worker. Missing or stale graph data fails explicitly and does not fall back to vector retrieval. Tests exercise the real local PPR ranking over a persisted SQLite graph snapshot while replacing only the external chat completion with a deterministic response. On 2026-10-03, the complete RAG Python suite passed 119 tests and `compileall` passed. This still does not prove live LLM-backed evaluation, external Embedding/Reranker/MinerU availability, or complete Yuxi functional parity.

Yuxi admin-only knowledge, file, graph, and evaluation-dataset export/delete routes now enforce the upstream admin/superadmin boundary; knowledge-base scoped evaluation upload/read continues to use resource permissions. Regular users retain the accessible-knowledge-base listing. Task list, detail, cancellation, and deletion enforce the same admin role requirement. The superadmin-only `/api/dashboard/stats/knowledge` route also matches upstream. On 2026-10-03, the complete local RAG suite passed 122 tests and compileall passed; admin, superadmin, and regular-user access were exercised across the protected routes.

The current-source route comparison parses Yuxi v0.7.3's knowledge, external-knowledge, evaluation, graph, and knowledge-dashboard routers and confirms all 77 upstream method/path operations have a local compatibility route; 16 additional local routes cover Geo workspace, task, upload-folder, and provider-test behavior. This confirms route-surface coverage only. An isolated current-source HTTP run on `:8012` used a temporary SQLite database and the real 1,528,947-byte, 49-page PDF: upload → parse → index completed with 67 chunks and 1,009 bbox source spans. BM25 debug retrieval returned 3 candidates, Fusion 3, Evidence 3, and 915 characters of Final Context; Vector and Rerank were skipped because no model endpoint/key was configured. `/health` returned 200.

After replacing the old process, the current source is now active on `:8010`; `/health` returned 200 and the Java `:8007` RAG proxy listed the 20 persisted knowledge bases. On the real 49-page PDF, direct `:8010` and Java-proxied debug retrieval returned matching results: BM25 38 candidates, Vector 0, Fusion 5, Rerank 0, five final Evidence records with page/bbox, and a 3,330-character Final Context. The embedded Yuxi UI returned the same five results; its PDF preview opened page 17 of 49 and displayed a red bbox over the matching source text. No Embedding, Reranker, MinerU, or LLM provider is configured, so those model calls remain unverified and the current retrieval acceptance is BM25-only. `npm run build` completed for both Yuxi and the host Vue app. At this check, `:8007` was the standalone local-auth/RAG development facade; the full business Spring Boot process was not active because Redis `:26379` was not listening. The RAG acceptance does not establish complete business API runtime parity or full functional parity for every Yuxi deployment feature.
